settings.heading: Getting a compounded medicine: what to expect
settings.body: If your doctor has suggested a compounded medicine, you probably have a few questions. What happens after you send the script? How much will it cost? Is it any different to take? This page covers the practical side, from your first contact with us to finishing the course.

settings.title: Paediatric
settings.body: Doses and forms sized for children
settings.detail: Children often need smaller doses than a tablet allows, or a form they can actually take. Where your child's prescriber asks for it, we can prepare a liquid in place of a tablet, adjust the strength, or add a flavour that makes taking it easier. We'll show you how to measure each dose before you leave.

settings.title: Geriatric
settings.detail: Swallowing can get harder with age, and crushing tablets isn't always a safe workaround. On a prescriber's order, we can prepare a medicine as a liquid, a thickened liquid at a set IDDSI level, or another form that suits the person. If they take several medicines, we're happy to talk with their carer or doctor about how it all fits together.

settings.title: Veterinary
settings.detail: Animals come in every size, and many won't take a tablet made for people. When a registered vet prescribes it, we can prepare a medicine at a strength that suits the animal's weight, in a form that's easier to give. If you're a pet owner, start with your vet. They can send the script straight to us.

settings.title: Alternative Medicine
settings.body: Less common prescriptions, checked case by case
settings.detail: Some prescriptions ask for natural-based ingredients or formulations you won't find on a pharmacy shelf. If your prescriber has written one, send it through and a pharmacist will check whether we can prepare it, and explain what's involved before anything is made. We only prepare these against a valid Australian prescription.

settings.title: Free-from formulas
settings.body: Without the ingredient you react to
settings.detail: Some commercial medicines contain lactose, gluten, dyes, sugar or preservatives that don't agree with everyone. If your prescriber asks for a version without a particular ingredient, we'll check whether it can be made that way and tell you plainly if it can't.

settings.title: Hard-to-find medicines
settings.body: When a product isn't available in Australia
settings.detail: Medicines are sometimes discontinued or short in supply. If your prescriber decides a compounded version is appropriate, we can look at whether it's practical to prepare. If a suitable commercial product is available, we'll tell you, because that's usually the better option.

settings.title: Something else
settings.body: Not sure where yours fits? Ask us
settings.detail: Every prescription is different. Tell us what you've been prescribed and a pharmacist will get back to you to talk through whether we can help.

settings.heading: When a standard medicine doesn't quite fit
settings.intro: Most people never need a compounded medicine. But sometimes the form, strength or ingredients of a commercial product don't suit the person taking it. If your doctor or vet thinks a compounded version is the right call, we prepare it to their prescription. These are the requests we see most.
settings.footnote: Compounded medicines are only prepared on a valid prescription for a named patient. Your prescriber decides whether one is right for you.

settings.title: Electrolyte Replacement Sachets
settings.body: Oral rehydration powder, low in sugar.

settings.title: Wound Irrigation Kit
settings.body: Sterile saline in single-use ampoules, for rinsing.

settings.heading: Everyday pharmacy lines, delivered
settings.lede: Alongside compounding, we stock a small range of over-the-counter products you can order online. No prescription needed. If you're not sure a product suits you, call or email and a pharmacist will help.
settings.label_line: Always read the label and follow the directions for use.

settings.question: Do I need a prescription?
settings.answer: For almost every medicine we compound, yes. Your doctor decides whether a compounded medicine is right and what it should contain.

settings.question: How long does it take?
settings.answer: Most medicines are ready within 1 to 2 business days of receiving a valid prescription. Some take longer, and we'll let you know when you order. Delivery time is extra.

settings.question: Are compounded medicines checked by the TGA?
settings.answer: No. The TGA does not evaluate compounded medicines for safety, quality or effectiveness before they're supplied. If a suitable TGA-approved medicine is available, it's generally the better choice, and your pharmacist may suggest it.

settings.question: Can I claim it on my private health insurance?
settings.answer: Some funds include a benefit for private prescriptions. We can give you an itemised receipt; check with your fund about what your policy covers.
